 Advertisement Unruly Logan Airport passenger tackled, arrested after trying to grab computer behind baggage counter
 Advertisement Updated: 10:42 PM EST Nov 14, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Arielle Mitropoulos Reporter Unruly Logan Airport passenger tackled, arrested after trying to grab computer behind baggage counter
 Updated: 10:42 PM EST Nov 14, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Arielle Mitropoulos Reporter EAST BOSTON, Mass. — An unruly passenger at Logan Airport was arrested after a heated confrontation over damaged luggage, amid growing frustrations over widespread flight delays and cancellations after a nationwide ground stop on Friday. 
 Witnesses said that the man became frustrated and attempted to grab a computer behind the American Airlines baggage support counter inside Terminal B on Saturday evening before another man tackled him. 
 Advertisement "He looked angry," said Rommel Marson, who said he witnessed the incident. "They tried to wrestle the guy until the police came."
 Massachusetts State Police identified the man to NewsCenter 5 as 43-year-old Andrew Kipchirchir from Boston. Authorities confirmed that he was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct and an outstanding warrant. 
 Boston Logan flights restart after FAA orders nationwide ground stop The incident occurred a day after the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop due to a telecommunications issue with the air traffic control system, leading to thousands of canceled flights. 
 "This is just such a big disaster," said Sandra Cornell, who, along with her sister Nellie, is trying to return to Arizona after a cruise. The sisters said they will be sleeping at the airport until their flight on Sunday. 
 "It's no fun. We've been provided cots, which is great. And a quiet place, so we appreciate all that," Sandra Cornell said. 
 Some passengers expressed frustration over the lack of support from airlines, including the absence of hotel vouchers. 
 "The biggest problem is they are not offering any accommodation, any food coupon, nothing," said passenger Mohammed Raihamuzzaman, who is trying to get back to Michigan.
 What passengers can expect now that nationwide ground stop has lifted While flights have resumed, the backlog continues to create challenges for travelers. Many are left uncertain about when they will finally reach their destinations. 
 "So they're just saying that it's not guaranteed. If we fly, it's good. If we don't fly, we have to rebook you," said Raihamuzzaman.
